title: 4.9 Modeling with Polynomial Functions

icans: I can write cubic functions given the x-intercepts and a point.
I can use finite differences to find the degree of a polynomial model.
I can use technology to find polynomial models for real-life data.

vocab: differences of ______________ y-values when the x-values are equally spaced
if the nth differences are ___________ (and nonzero), the data fit a polynomial of degree n
_____________ that finds the polynomial of a given degree that best fits data

blocks.p: Square pyramids of cubes: 1 layer = 1 cube, 2 layers = 1 + 4 cubes, 3 layers = 1 + 4 + 9 cubes, …

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Cubic from x-intercepts: Cubic from x-intercepts p, q, r: f(x) = _______________. Use another point to find ______.

blocks.stem: Write the cubic function whose graph has x-intercepts −2, 1, and 3 and passes through (0, −6).
Use finite differences to find the degree of the polynomial function that fits the data. Then find the function.
Write the cubic function with x-intercepts −1, 2, and 4 that passes through (1, 12).
Find the degree of the polynomial that fits the data:  x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5;  y = 3, 6, 11, 18, 27.
Write the cubic function with x-intercepts −3, 0, and 2 that passes through (1, −8).

tickets.stem: The third differences of a data set are constant. What is the degree of the polynomial that fits the data?
